title: Researchers are getting tired of OpenAI gatekeeping its breakthroughs
slides: Why are researchers turning against OpenAI's secrecy?
Its breakthrough models stay closed to outside scientists
Yet leaked evals show narrow gains on some benchmarks
Independent labs now replicate frontier results at lower cost
Demand open weights before citing closed-model claims
thread_text:
1. The fight over closed AI

OpenAI's newest models remain hidden from outside scientists, and researchers are now demanding open weights before trusting benchmark claims.

2. Leaked evals, narrow wins

Internal evaluation leaks show the models gain only a few points on standard tests — far less than the marketing suggests.

3. Independent labs catch up

Smaller teams are now replicating frontier results at a fraction of the cost, raising questions about what the secrecy is really protecting.

4. Secrecy blocks verification

Without open weights, external researchers can't reproduce or stress-test the claims, turning peer review into a PR exercise.

5. Ask for the weights

Next time you see a closed-model benchmark, ask: where are the weights? If there's no answer, treat the number as a rumor.

Researchers are now demanding open weights before trusting any benchmark claim from OpenAI's newest models. 🔍

Meanwhile, smaller independent labs are replicating frontier results at a fraction of the cost. 🧪

Without access to the weights, outside scientists can't reproduce or stress-test the claims — peer review becomes a PR exercise.

If you publish or cite benchmark numbers, this affects you: you may be repeating unverified marketing as fact. 📊

Next time you see a closed-model benchmark, ask: where are the weights? If there's no answer, treat the number as a rumor. 🤔
